latestTerminalSummary:
Completed r136 as **PREFREEZE / no nominee**. No theorem scope was frozen, no gate assigned, and no campaign count added.

The [mathematical notes](/home/mj-kang/Documents/Dev/math/openai-proof-research/frontier/campaigns/2026-10-14/fresh-structural-discovery-r136/packet/public/derivations.md) establish:

- A K4 example with optimal single-tree thinness **15/13**, versus **5/3** when exact edge marginals must be preserved.
- A triangle family whose ratio approaches two, and a proof that joining these examples at vertices cannot amplify the gap.
- A precise sufficient bisection condition for universal exact-marginal thin-tree distributions. That condition remains unproved: preserving an **exact partition into spanning trees** through cut-controlled splitting is the missing operation.

The [handoff report](/home/mj-kang/Documents/Dev/math/openai-proof-research/frontier/campaigns/2026-10-14/fresh-structural-discovery-r136/REPORT.md) records the strongest source/primary comparison, remaining obligations, partial and late reads, and preservation limits.

Artifact verification succeeded: 105 payload files, 40 authenticated source blobs, five primary versions, and 29 stable originals unchanged. All eight copied integrity controls behaved as expected. These are artifact checks, not mathematical gates.
